name: Expecting var to be block scoped
explanation: var is scoped to the whole function, not to the loop body. Every closure created in a var loop shares the same i, which already holds its final value when the closures run. let creates a new binding for each iteration.

name: Thinking a closure copies values
explanation: A closure keeps a reference to the variable itself, not a snapshot of its value. Each call to next() updates the same count, so the second call returns 2.

name: Mutating an array while iterating over it
explanation: for...of walks the array by index. splice shifts every later element one place left, so the element that moves into the current index is skipped. Build a new array instead, for example nums.filter((n) => n % 2 !== 0).

name: Off-by-one on array bounds
explanation: An array of length n has indexes 0 to n - 1. xs[xs.length] is undefined, and a loop condition of i <= xs.length runs one step too far. Use i < xs.length, and xs[xs.length - 1] for the last element.
